responseBinding.correctOptionText: To avoid judging fairness only among programme participants

rows.sourceExcerpt: It also keeps unenrolled patients and unmet needs visible.
rows.rationale: La pregunta pide «Why should an evaluation keep unenrolled patients and unmet needs visible?» y la clave es «To avoid judging fairness only among programme participants». La evidencia dice «It also keeps unenrolled patients and unmet needs visible.». La coincidencia semántica se apoya en «unenrolled», «patients», «unmet», «needs», «visible»: esos elementos enlazan el foco de la pregunta y la opción con la información del pasaje, mientras las demás opciones carecen de ese vínculo en el tramo citado.
rows.sourceLedgerRationale: Keeping non-participants and unmet need in view prevents an assessment of fairness from being limited to those enrolled.

responseBinding.questionText: Which statement best summarises the writer's conclusion?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Programmes should be judged through explicit design and system-wide evidence.

rows.sourceExcerpt: Community paramedicine should be judged as a designed system, not as a job title with assumed effects.
rows.rationale: La pregunta pide «Which statement best summarises the writer's conclusion?» y la clave es «Programmes should be judged through explicit design and system-wide evidence.». La evidencia dice «Community paramedicine should be judged as a designed system, not as a job title with assumed effects.». La coincidencia semántica se apoya en «judged», «system»: esos elementos enlazan el foco de la pregunta y la opción con la información del pasaje, mientras las demás opciones carecen de ese vínculo en el tramo citado.
rows.sourceLedgerRationale: The conclusion requires explicit programme design and evidence across the service pathway.

responseBinding.questionText: Destination country: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Yes, Canada. The American address belongs to another relative. This parcel is going to Vancouver, and the postcode on the label is the Canadian one.

responseBinding.questionText: Main item: wool ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: It is a wool scarf. I nearly wrote just gift, but the help note said to name the item, so wool scarf would be accurate.

responseBinding.questionText: Parcel weight: ______ kg

bindings.audiblePhrase: The scale shows one point eight kilograms. That replaces your estimate of two and a half, which included a bag you are keeping.

responseBinding.questionText: Declared value: NZ$ ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Please record one point eight kilograms, then. The scarf cost sixty dollars and the puzzle was fifteen, so the total declared value is seventy-five New Zealand dollars.

responseBinding.questionText: Sender street: Aroha ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Aroha Lane is correct. Road was my old address. The house number remains fourteen, which is probably why I missed the error.

responseBinding.questionText: Selected service: ______ Track

bindings.audiblePhrase: My cousin works away from home on weekdays, so the signature could cause difficulty. Economy Track is fine; I care more about being able to follow the parcel than about the shortest time.

responseBinding.questionText: Which item must Moana remove from the parcel?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Before payment, let us check every item against the current destination list. You have the scarf, a small wooden puzzle, a watercolour set and this jar of honey. The list on my screen says the honey cannot be accepted in this parcel.

responseBinding.questionText: Why did Moana think the removed item might be accepted?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: She had sent it within New Zealand.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Then I will take the honey out. I have posted it within New Zealand before, so I assumed it would be acceptable overseas as well.

responseBinding.questionText: How will the final parcel labels be produced?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The counter printer will produce them.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Do not add another handwritten label. The counter printer produces the final address and customs labels together. I will place them on the largest face of the box and leave the seams clear.

responseBinding.questionText: What does Callum say remains Moana’s responsibility?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Exactly. Confirm the declaration, and I will print the labels today. Keep the tracking receipt, but remember that the sender remains responsible for an accurate contents statement.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the changing room?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Look at the plan. From the entrance, turn right before reception and follow the path to the eastern wall. The changing room is the long public room immediately south of the smaller staff store.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the first-aid room?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Return to reception and take the path on your left. Pass the ticket office nearest reception, then turn slightly north. The first-aid room is below the centre of the shallow end. Do not continue to the far western boundary.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the accessible ramp?

bindings.audiblePhrase: From first aid, continue north-west along the boundary. The accessible ramp is directly below the shallow end, at the far western edge. Nearby steps are shorter, but only the ramp has a handrail and gradual slope.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the tide gate?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The main lap lanes occupy the centre of the pool. The tide gate is beyond their northern end, just outside the upper-right corner of the lane area. Staff operate it; swimmers must never try to move it, even when the water appears calm.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the family deck?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Now look south-east of reception. Two possible places sit near the street entrance. The family deck is the more central one, with benches and a clear view of the shallow area. The other place, farther east near the boundary, is only a delivery bay.

responseBinding.questionText: Where are the equipment racks?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Finally, the equipment racks are south-west of reception, closer to the street entrance than the first-aid room. Personal property belongs in lockers; the racks are for kickboards and pool wheelchairs.

responseBinding.questionText: What colour flag shows that a section is closed?

bindings.audiblePhrase: If a section closes, staff raise a red flag beside reception. The electronic sign repeats the message, but the flag is the quickest answer if you are already on the deck. A yellow flag means extra caution, not closure.

responseBinding.questionText: What should visitors read before using the northern path?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Before walking to the northern path, read the tide board. It displays the staff inspection time as well as the expected tide. A phone forecast may be useful before travelling, but the tide board gives the decision for this facility.

responseBinding.questionText: What should swimmers use when entering by the ramp?

bindings.audiblePhrase: At the accessible ramp, enter facing forward and use the handrail. The painted edge is a visual guide; it is not something to grip. If you need the pool wheelchair, ask at reception rather than moving one from the equipment rack yourself.

responseBinding.questionText: What do children need if they enter outside a coached lesson?

bindings.audiblePhrase: To recap: a red flag shows closure, read the tide board, use the ramp handrail, and remember that children require adult supervision. We will now walk the safe southern route.

responseBinding.questionText: Which source will the trainees use to check earliest online appearance?

bindings.audiblePhrase: First, we need the earliest known online appearance. I will run a reverse-image search. If an older copy exists, the current post may be recycling an image from another event.

responseBinding.questionText: Which source will the trainees use to check camera time?

bindings.audiblePhrase: For the camera time, I will inspect the image metadata. A timestamp can be altered or stripped, so it is a clue rather than proof.

responseBinding.questionText: Which source will the trainees use to check weather at the claimed hour?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The sky in the photograph is bright, yet the caption says heavy rain was falling at seven. We can compare that visual clue with a weather archive for the claimed place and hour.

responseBinding.questionText: Which source will the trainees use to check fixed landmarks?

bindings.audiblePhrase: For location, the shop sign is blurred, but the mural and the shape of the junction are distinctive. A street map with recent imagery should let us compare those fixed landmarks.

responseBinding.questionText: Which source will the trainees use to check first-hand context and permission?

bindings.audiblePhrase: I will contact the original uploader, ask what they saw and request the uncompressed file. We can also confirm permission.

responseBinding.questionText: What does the reverse-image search reveal?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The picture appeared online eighteen months earlier.

bindings.audiblePhrase: I have the reverse search result. The same photograph appeared eighteen months ago on a community blog in Halifax. It was cropped differently, but the bus, awning and water pattern are identical.

responseBinding.questionText: What conclusion do they draw from the missing location metadata?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The image does not establish its location.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Missing coordinates do not prove manipulation. Devices or platforms may omit them. The file does not establish location; that is all we can conclude.

responseBinding.questionText: What corrects Declan’s first interpretation of the red vehicle?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The correction matters. Colour suggested public transport, but the visible company logo and route context are stronger evidence.

responseBinding.questionText: What do the trainees decide to do next?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Refer the publication decision to the editor.

bindings.audiblePhrase: We should hold the image, preserve our evidence and alert the news editor. The editor can choose a correction, verification note or no article.

responseBinding.questionText: Which statement best describes their verified finding?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: It is a genuine older image with a false time and place.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Exactly. The strongest result is not simply fake image. It is a genuine older photograph presented with a false current location and time. That description is both more precise and easier to defend.

responseBinding.questionText: Cryoconite begins with fine mineral ______ and organic particles.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Cryoconite begins with fine mineral dust and organic particles deposited by wind, meltwater or nearby exposed ground. The material is visibly darker than clean snow or ice, and researchers compare the two surfaces carefully.

responseBinding.questionText: A dark patch has lower ______ than clean bright ice.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The relevant property is albedo, the proportion of incoming radiation a surface reflects. Clean bright ice has relatively high albedo, while a dark patch has lower albedo. We will return later to the physical consequence of that contrast.

responseBinding.questionText: As a hole forms, ______ collects around the particles.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Dark particles can settle into a shallow cavity while remaining exposed to light from above. Meltwater collects around them, and the wet sediment creates a small habitat whose depth and outline can change during the season.

responseBinding.questionText: Microbial substances help bind particles into ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The sediment is not biologically inert. Bacteria, algae and other microorganisms live among the grains. Sticky substances produced by microbes help bind fine particles into granules; the resulting structure is compact rather than a completely loose layer of dust.

responseBinding.questionText: In very cold settings, a lid of ______ may form above the water.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Conditions differ among glaciers. On temperate ice, water may move through open surface channels. In very cold polar settings, a lid of ice can form above the liquid water for part of the season.

responseBinding.questionText: Material accidentally introduced during sampling is called ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: That final problem is contamination. Good field practice records the location and physical form before collection, then uses clean tools. Care reduces introduced material, although natural differences between holes still remain.

responseBinding.questionText: Why can a dark patch deepen the ice beneath it?

bindings.audiblePhrase: We can now explain why the darker material may deepen the ice beneath it. Its lower albedo means that it absorbs more incoming energy than bright ice, so local melting can proceed more quickly.

responseBinding.questionText: What does the lecturer say about a hole with an ice lid?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: It is relatively closed but not permanently sealed.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The ice lid also needs careful interpretation. It can make a hole relatively closed for a period, but the system is not permanently sealed. Light can pass through ice, and later melting can reopen a connection.

responseBinding.questionText: Why are replicate samples valuable?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: They represent spatial variation better than one hole.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Replicate samples are valuable because they represent spatial variation better than one hole. Several samples from a defined area reveal whether a result is common or simply a feature of one unusual cavity.

responseBinding.questionText: Which study design does the lecturer recommend?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Biological sampling combined with physical and hydrological observations

bindings.audiblePhrase: The strongest study design therefore combines biological sampling with physical and hydrological observations. Microbial groups and pigments are interpreted alongside depth, reflectance, water routes, temperature and the timing of lid formation.
